title: Redwood Demo Runthrough (internal dry run) - v1 deck + live tenant
summary: Internal dry-run of the standard sales demo (deck v1 + live Console walkthrough) with AE (Avery), SE/demo owner (Markus), and PMM (Soojin). Team reviewed timing, clarity of the narrative, and brittle live steps: seeded dashboard freshness, quota/429 risk during streaming, model pinning/fallback explanation, and the Optimize/batching story dragging. Key feedback: move the “why Redwood / production economics” punchline earlier, tighten jargon (KV cache, continuous batching), and define a crisp backup mode (screenshots/recording + canned outputs) for every live step. Agreed to add a pre-demo healthcheck command, simplify the tool-calling example, and adjust the handoff cues between AE and SE.
topics: Deck flow: problem → why now → platform → live demo modules
Live demo steps: streaming chat, structured output, tool calling, retries
Console tour: cost/latency breakdown, traces, error analysis, rollouts
Production economics: batching/caching toggles and “what changed” explanation
Reliability: model pinning + safe fallback routing (region/model family)
Failure modes: empty dashboards, 429 throttles, auth/RBAC, model not available
Objection handling: Dedicated predictability, VPC/Private narrative, security FAQ pointers
questions: Do we want to lead with “unified inference across hosted/dedicated/private” or “production economics” as the headline?
How much of the Console tour is safe to do live vs screenshots (rollouts view seems flaky)?
Should the demo app use OpenAI-compat endpoint or native Redwood SDK in the live code snippet?
What’s the single sentence explanation of fallback routing that won’t trigger a reliability debate?
What are the approved benchmark numbers/caveats we can say out loud (and which should stay in appendix only)?
action_items: Markus Klein — Add a 1-command pre-demo healthcheck output (quota, model availability, dashboard freshness) and paste into run-of-show — Due 2025-11-11
Avery Johnson — Rewrite the first 3 minutes to ask 2 discovery questions and then land the “why now / serving is the bottleneck” line faster — Due 2025-11-08
Soojin Lee — Update talk track to reduce Optimize jargon; rename verbally to “cost/perf controls” and provide 2 approved phrases — Due 2025-11-12
Markus Klein — Simplify tool-calling example to one function with deterministic output; add a canned output fallback — Due 2025-11-13
Soojin Lee — Add explicit handoff cues in speaker notes (AE→SE and SE→AE) and mark optional branches for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private — Due 2025-11-12
Avery Johnson — Create a 20-min exec variant slide order + what to skip list — Due 2025-11-10
Markus Klein — Document the brittle Console screens (rollouts view, traces filter) and provide screenshots for backup mode — Due 2025-11-15
next_steps: Run the demo again with the 20-min exec variant and time it strictly.
Add backup mode artifacts: screenshots + short recording + canned outputs for each live step.
Pin demo routes to known-good model versions and verify fallback explanation in talk track.
Confirm synthetic traffic generator schedule so dashboards aren’t empty.
Publish v1 run-of-show doc with pre-demo checklist and post-demo reset steps.
transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2025-11-06
Start time: 4:00 PM PT
Duration: 47 min
Title: Redwood Demo Runthrough (internal dry run) - v1 deck + live tenant
Attendees: Avery Johnson (AE), Markus Klein (SE / demo technical owner), Soojin Lee (PMM)

Summary (auto)
- Dry run of full 30-min demo with live Console.
- Feedback on pacing, messaging, and brittle live steps.
- Identified backup paths for common failure modes.

Transcript
[00:00] Avery Johnson: Alright, cool. This is the internal run-through. Goal is: can we do the full story in 30, and then what do we cut for 20.
[00:09] Soojin Lee: Yep. And I’m mostly listening for where we lose people, like where the narrative drags or gets too… inside baseball.
[00:16] Markus Klein: I’ll drive the live steps. Also calling out anything brittle with the tenant. I had one weird dashboard thing earlier, so we’ll see.

[00:27] Avery Johnson: Okay, starting on slide one. “LLMs are easy to prototype, hard to serve.” I usually ask: what’s your current model stack and where do you run it.
[00:38] Soojin Lee: I like the question, but you’re asking it before you’ve earned it. Like, maybe do one sentence of context first.
[00:45] Avery Johnson: Got it. So: “Teams are shipping more LLM features, and the bottleneck is serving—latency, cost, reliability.” Then question.
[00:55] Markus Klein: Yeah. And it sets up why we’re not just “a model provider.”

[01:03] Avery Johnson: Slide two: why now. Open models, hardware changing, you can’t re-platform every quarter.
[01:12] Soojin Lee: Can we say “model landscape is moving” instead of “open ecosystem” every time? It’s getting repetitive.
[01:18] Avery Johnson: Sure. Slide three is “Redwood is unified inference: hosted, dedicated, private.”
[01:25] Soojin Lee: I’m torn. The other headline is “production economics.” What do we want as the hook?
[01:31] Markus Klein: In the field, “economics” resonates when they’re already feeling pain. If cold start, “unified across environments” is simpler.
[01:41] Avery Johnson: Maybe we land “serving is the moat” then the hook is “make serving predictable.” Then we can branch.

[01:54] Avery Johnson: Okay, moving to the live section. Markus, you ready to share screen?
[01:58] Markus Klein: Yup, sharing.

[02:04] Markus Klein: I’m in the demo org. First thing: we show the API call with streaming. We’ll use the demo app.
[02:11] Soojin Lee: Before you run it, say what they’re about to see: streaming tokens, retries, and a structured output. Otherwise it just looks like any chat.
[02:20] Avery Johnson: Good call. I’ll tee it up: “We’ll make a request, stream, then we’ll toggle cost controls and see what changes.”

[02:30] Markus Klein: Running the “Customer support agent” scenario. It calls chat completions with streaming. Okay, you see tokens coming in.
[02:38] Avery Johnson: And we should mention: same API works hosted, dedicated, private. Not three SDKs.
[02:44] Soojin Lee: Keep it short. One sentence. Don’t re-open it.

[02:51] Markus Klein: Now structured output. We ask for JSON with fields: “category”, “priority”, “suggested_reply”.
[02:59] Avery Johnson: Nice. This is where I say: “In prod you want deterministic-ish shape, not just text.”
[03:05] Soojin Lee: Avoid “deterministic-ish.” Just say “schema-validated output.”
[03:09] Avery Johnson: Fair.

[03:13] Markus Klein: Tool calling. Our example calls “lookup_order_status.” It’s a stub in the demo app.
[03:19] Soojin Lee: This is brittle. If the tool returns something unexpected, we’re stuck in front of a customer.
[03:24] Markus Klein: Agree. I can make it one tool, one path, fixed output.
[03:28] Avery Johnson: Also: do we need tool calling AND structured output? It’s like feature salad.
[03:34] Soojin Lee: Exactly. Pick one as the star. Tool calling is cool but it can derail.
[03:39] Markus Klein: We can keep tool calling as an optional branch if they ask.

[03:46] Avery Johnson: Okay, now “retries.” Markus, can you simulate an error?
[03:50] Markus Klein: Yeah, I can flip the rate limit low. But that’s also risky; could create 429s that persist.
[03:57] Soojin Lee: Maybe don’t create a failure live. Just show the code snippet and say we have built-in retry guidance.
[04:03] Avery Johnson: Or show an existing trace where there was a retry.
[04:07] Markus Klein: That’s better. I can pull a trace from the synthetic traffic.

[04:13] Markus Klein: Switching to Console. Here’s the project dashboard.
[04:18] (pause)
[04:19] Markus Klein: Uh. It’s loading but… the graphs are empty.
[04:23] Avery Johnson: Okay, this is exactly the thing we’re trying to prevent.
[04:26] Soojin Lee: Yep. This is the worst feeling in a live demo.

[04:30] Markus Klein: Let me change the time range. It’s defaulting to “Last 15 minutes.” If the synthetic job ran an hour ago, we’re dead.
[04:38] Avery Johnson: That’s a product thing but for the demo we need a guardrail.
[04:41] Markus Klein: Switching to “Last 24 hours.” Okay, now we have data.
[04:47] Soojin Lee: In the talk track: say out loud “we’ll look at last 24 hours” so it doesn’t look like you’re scrambling.

[04:55] Avery Johnson: What do we do if there’s truly no data? Like the job didn’t run.
[04:59] Markus Klein: Backup mode: screenshots, and we run the synthetic generator in the background. But that takes like 2–3 minutes.
[05:06] Soojin Lee: Then we need a pre-demo check that confirms “dashboards populated.”
[05:10] Markus Klein: Yep. Healthcheck command should assert ingestion freshness.

[05:16] Avery Johnson: Okay, now that data’s there. Markus, show token-level breakdown.
[05:20] Markus Klein: Here’s the cost view. You can break down prompt tokens vs completion tokens. Latency p50/p95 by route.
[05:27] Avery Johnson: This is the “production economics” moment. I say: “We don’t hide the knobs. We show you what’s expensive.”
[05:35] Soojin Lee: That’s good. But don’t say “knobs” too much. Maybe “controls” or “levers.”

[05:44] Markus Klein: Now the batching toggle. In the route config, we can enable continuous batching.
[05:50] Soojin Lee: Careful. “Continuous batching” can confuse. Just say “automatic batching.”
[05:56] Markus Klein: Okay. Turning it on. The synthetic traffic is still hitting, so we should see p95 change.
[06:03] Avery Johnson: And we narrate the tradeoff: slightly higher tail latency sometimes, lower cost per token.
[06:09] Soojin Lee: Also say “you can choose policies by endpoint.” Like chat vs background summarization.

[06:17] Markus Klein: Here’s caching. Prefix caching on. KV cache reuse. (It might transcribe that wrong, whatever.)
[06:23] Soojin Lee: Don’t say “K V cache” unless asked. It’s too deep.
[06:28] Avery Johnson: I’ll simplify: “We reuse shared prefixes so repeated prompts get cheaper.”

[06:36] Markus Klein: Switching to traces. Here’s a request trace: model, tokens, latency, and you can see a retry event.
[06:43] Avery Johnson: Great. That solves the earlier retry demo. We can point to it instead of breaking stuff live.
[06:48] Soojin Lee: Also highlight: “this works across hosted and dedicated.” That’s the tie-in.

[06:56] Avery Johnson: Okay, reliability module. Markus, show fallback routing.
[06:59] Markus Klein: Yeah, so this route is pinned to “rw-llama-3.1-70b” version something. If it’s unavailable, we can fall back to a compatible variant.
[07:10] Soojin Lee: That sentence is a landmine. Customers hear “fallback” and think “my quality changes.”
[07:15] Avery Johnson: We need a safer framing: “graceful degradation policies you control.”
[07:20] Markus Klein: Exactly. We can say: “you define allowed fallbacks; default is none unless you enable.”
[07:27] Soojin Lee: Yes. Say: “opt-in.”

[07:34] Markus Klein: In Console, rollouts view… this is the one that sometimes gets flaky.
[07:39] Avery Johnson: If it’s flaky, we should screenshot it and keep live optional.
[07:43] Soojin Lee: Agree. Make it appendix live. Not core path.

[07:50] Markus Klein: Opening it now. Okay, it loaded. Canary 10% vs 90%. You can compare latency and cost.
[07:58] Avery Johnson: This is great, but we’re at like minute eight and we haven’t talked security or private yet.
[08:03] Soojin Lee: That’s okay. Security is a branch. Don’t force it in every time.
[08:07] Avery Johnson: But in enterprise calls, they ask early.
[08:10] Soojin Lee: Then we add a “security reviewer” branch after the first live win.

[08:18] Markus Klein: One more reliability thing: region failover. If EU region streaming is flaky, we can route to US.
[08:25] Avery Johnson: Mentioning EU streaming being flaky is probably not something we want to say.
[08:29] Markus Klein: Yeah, sorry. I meant as a general capability: multi-region policies.
[08:33] Soojin Lee: “Resilience across regions” is fine. Don’t cite a bug.

[08:40] Avery Johnson: Timing check. If we do all this plus security, we’re over 30.
[08:45] Soojin Lee: We need a standard spine: (1) one API call streaming + structured, (2) console cost/latency, (3) reliability policy. Everything else optional.
[08:56] Markus Klein: I can speed up the live steps by having tabs pre-opened.
[09:00] Avery Johnson: Yes, and less clicking.

[09:06] Soojin Lee: Quick note: the “Optimize” name is confusing. When you say “Redwood Optimize,” people think it’s a separate product or consulting.
[09:14] Avery Johnson: I’ve felt that. They ask “is that an add-on?”
[09:17] Markus Klein: It is kind of an add-on.
[09:20] Soojin Lee: Right, but in the demo, call it “cost/performance controls” and mention “some advanced recommendations are add-on.”
[09:29] Avery Johnson: Okay. I’ll stop saying “Optimize” as the verb.

[09:36] Markus Klein: Want me to run the “economics toggle” again but with numbers?
[09:40] Avery Johnson: Yes, but keep it high level. We don’t want to be pinned to exact cents per million tokens.
[09:46] Soojin Lee: We need approved ranges and caveats. Don’t improvise.

[09:53] Markus Klein: Okay, showing relative change. “Batching on” reduces cost per token by X percent in this synthetic workload.
[10:00] Avery Johnson: I’ll say: “in real workloads, we often see meaningful reductions; we’ll validate in your prompts.”
[10:06] Soojin Lee: Good. Tie it to evals and prompt sets.

[10:12] Markus Klein: That’s another demo module: prompt sets and regression alerts.
[10:16] Avery Johnson: Optional. It’s cool for ML platform persona.
[10:19] Soojin Lee: But don’t overload. Mention it exists and offer to show after.

[10:26] Avery Johnson: Let’s jump to security narrative quickly. Soojin, can you critique my phrasing.
[10:31] Avery Johnson: “For enterprises: SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, retention controls, plus private deployments in your VPC or on-prem.”
[10:41] Soojin Lee: That’s fine. Then say “we’ll share the security FAQ and SOC2 under NDA” or whatever the process is.
[10:48] Markus Klein: And say “demo data is synthetic” if we show logs.
[10:52] Avery Johnson: Right.

[10:56] Markus Klein: Also we should be careful showing audit logs live. It can reveal internal emails or key IDs.
[11:02] Soojin Lee: For the demo tenant, audit logs should be sanitized, but still—maybe screenshots only.
[11:07] Avery Johnson: I’ll keep it narrative with one screenshot.

[11:12] Markus Klein: Back to Console: RBAC settings. I can show roles.
[11:15] Avery Johnson: That’s the RBAC misconfig failure mode. If it’s wrong, we lose.
[11:20] Markus Klein: Exactly. Another reason for healthcheck: verify role mapping.
[11:25] Soojin Lee: Don’t show RBAC live unless asked.

[11:31] Avery Johnson: Let’s talk about the brittle steps list. What are top three.
[11:35] Markus Klein: One: dashboards empty, like we just saw. Two: quota/rate limits causing 429 mid-stream. Three: model not available if catalog changes or region capacity.
[11:47] Soojin Lee: And auth. Someone’s key expired.
[11:49] Markus Klein: Yep. Key rotation.

[11:53] Avery Johnson: For 429: can we set quotas high for demo and rely on rate limiting at the demo app level?
[12:00] Markus Klein: We can, but it risks noisy neighbor if we run parallel demos. Better: per-demo project isolation.
[12:07] Soojin Lee: Sales will not remember to create new projects manually.
[12:10] Markus Klein: That’s why we need provisioning automation.

[12:15] Avery Johnson: For model availability: what’s our line? “We pin versions.”
[12:19] Markus Klein: Yes. “We pin to a known-good model version; fallbacks are pre-approved.”
[12:25] Soojin Lee: Add “we’ll never surprise you with a silent model change.” That’s a good differentiation.
[12:31] Avery Johnson: Nice.

[12:36] Markus Klein: Also: streaming disconnects. Rare but if it happens once, it’s memorable.
[12:42] Avery Johnson: What do we do?
[12:44] Markus Klein: Backup is: switch to non-streaming output for that call, or show a recorded clip.
[12:49] Soojin Lee: Add it to run-of-show: “If streaming stalls, click to backup clip.”

[12:56] Avery Johnson: Okay. Now, I want to rehearse handoff cues. When do I pass to Markus.
[13:02] Soojin Lee: You set context and desired outcome. Markus executes the live thing. Then you pull back to value.
[13:10] Avery Johnson: So: I say “we’ll do one request, then show cost/latency.” Markus runs the request. Then I say “that’s dev-first; now ops view.”
[13:20] Markus Klein: Perfect.

[13:23] Avery Johnson: For Dedicated vs hosted: where do we insert.
[13:26] Soojin Lee: One slide or one sentence after the API win: “If you need predictable throughput and isolation, Dedicated.” Then stop.
[13:35] Markus Klein: And if they ask “noisy neighbor,” we emphasize reserved pools.
[13:40] Avery Johnson: Good.

[13:44] Soojin Lee: Also procurement: don’t bring up pricing too early.
[13:48] Avery Johnson: I only do “we’re usage-based and reserved capacity” at the end.
[13:52] Soojin Lee: Great.

[13:55] Markus Klein: Should we do the embeddings/rerank scenario in the core demo?
[13:59] Avery Johnson: Not in the standard 30. That’s for search use cases.
[14:04] Soojin Lee: Agree. Keep the base demo “chat + ops.”

[14:10] Avery Johnson: Let’s practice the “why Redwood” line in one breath.
[14:13] Avery Johnson: “Redwood gives you a production runtime plus the operational tooling so inference is predictable: you can see cost and latency per route, roll out safely, and set fallbacks you control—across hosted, dedicated, or private deployments.”
[14:28] Soojin Lee: That’s good. Maybe cut “production runtime plus.” Just say “a unified inference platform.”
[14:33] Markus Klein: It’s fine but keep it short.

[14:37] Avery Johnson: Okay, now we’re going to do the 20-min exec variant. What do we cut.
[14:42] Soojin Lee: Cut rollouts view live, cut tool calling, cut caching jargon. Keep one killer graph: cost vs latency and the lever.
[14:52] Markus Klein: And have a screenshot for rollouts.

[14:56] Avery Johnson: What about private deployment narrative. Execs ask.
[15:00] Soojin Lee: One architecture slide screenshot and one sentence: “control plane private, customer-managed networking, KMS.”
[15:08] Markus Klein: Also emphasize “same API.”

[15:12] Avery Johnson: Cool. Now, do we have any weird words we should avoid.
[15:16] Soojin Lee: “KV cache,” “kernel selection,” “quantization-friendly execution path.” If asked, great, but otherwise no.
[15:25] Markus Klein: I’ll restrain myself.

[15:28] Avery Johnson: Let’s jump back to the Console and simulate the narrative without clicking.
[15:33] Markus Klein: Okay. “Here’s your ops view: usage, latency p95, error rate, token mix.”
[15:39] Avery Johnson: “And we can attribute spend to the endpoints that matter.”
[15:44] Soojin Lee: Nice.

[15:47] Markus Klein: “If we turn on automatic batching for background summarization, costs drop, and interactive chat stays low latency.”
[15:55] Avery Johnson: Great.

[15:57] Soojin Lee: One more thing: define “demo success criteria.” Like, what’s the promise.
[16:03] Avery Johnson: Promise is: we can run the demo in 30, consistent, no weird failures.
[16:07] Markus Klein: And reset in minutes.
[16:10] Soojin Lee: Exactly. “We’re not improvising.”

[16:15] Avery Johnson: Okay, what broke last time in the field.
[16:18] Markus Klein: Dashboards empty. Streaming got weird once. Another time, a model name changed and the route didn’t match.
[16:27] Soojin Lee: That’s why we need a pinned config and a regression check.

[16:33] Avery Johnson: How do we explain fallback without sounding like we’re hiding outages.
[16:38] Markus Klein: We say: “You choose a policy. Default is strict pin. If you opt-in, we can degrade gracefully so your app stays up.”
[16:47] Soojin Lee: Good. And add: “we track it, you can alert on it.”

[16:53] Avery Johnson: Great. Next: objection handling. If they say “why not Bedrock.”
[16:58] Soojin Lee: We say: “If you’re all-in on AWS, it can work. Redwood differentiates on performance economics and unified ops across environments.”
[17:08] Avery Johnson: And “model flexibility.”
[17:10] Markus Klein: Also “transparent per-route metrics.”

[17:15] Avery Johnson: If they say “why not OpenAI.”
[17:18] Soojin Lee: Don’t bash. Say: “Great models, but teams hit cost/latency and deployment constraints; Redwood gives control and optional private.”

[17:27] Markus Klein: If they bring up Together or Anyscale.
[17:30] Avery Johnson: Similar. “We focus on production tooling, rollouts, fallbacks, and consistent experience.”
[17:36] Soojin Lee: Yep.

[17:40] Avery Johnson: I want to fix the dragging part. Where did it drag today.
[17:44] Soojin Lee: From minute 9 to 14, we were deep in “Optimize” and toggles. It needs a single crisp example, not a tour.
[17:54] Avery Johnson: So: one toggle, one outcome, then move on.
[17:57] Markus Klein: I can pre-load the “before vs after” dashboard panel.

[18:02] Avery Johnson: Perfect. Also, fewer product names.
[18:06] Soojin Lee: Yes. Say “Console,” say “API,” and then only mention Dedicated/Private if relevant.

[18:13] Markus Klein: Should we show the code snippet live?
[18:16] Avery Johnson: I usually paste the curl / SDK snippet in the deck.
[18:20] Soojin Lee: Better: screenshot of the snippet. Live coding is a trap.
[18:26] Markus Klein: Agreed.

[18:29] Avery Johnson: Okay, backup mode requirements. For each live step, we need a screenshot and a canned output.
[18:36] Soojin Lee: And a short recording. Like 60–90 seconds.
[18:40] Markus Klein: I can record once the tenant is stable.

[18:45] Avery Johnson: Let’s list live steps in order.
[18:48] Markus Klein: Step 1: streaming chat response. Step 2: structured output JSON. Step 3: Console cost/latency dashboard. Step 4: trace with retry. Step 5: route policy showing pin + optional fallback.
[19:02] Soojin Lee: Optional steps: rollouts, tool calling, security screenshots.

[19:08] Avery Johnson: Great. For each, backup.
[19:10] Markus Klein: Yep.

[19:13] Soojin Lee: Also add a “what to say if something breaks” line. Like scripted.
[19:18] Avery Johnson: “Sometimes telemetry takes a minute; we also have a recorded view.”
[19:23] Soojin Lee: Exactly.

[19:27] Markus Klein: But we should avoid saying “sometimes.” Just smoothly switch.
[19:31] Avery Johnson: Right. “Here’s the view” and we show screenshot.

[19:35] Avery Johnson: Anything else on timing.
[19:37] Soojin Lee: The beginning is still too long. You spent 4 minutes before showing anything. Aim to show tokens streaming by minute 3.
[19:48] Avery Johnson: Okay. I’ll cut intro slides.
[19:51] Markus Klein: I can be ready earlier with the app open.

[19:55] Avery Johnson: Great. Let’s do a quick re-run of the first three minutes as practice.
[20:00] Avery Johnson: “Quick context: LLM features are shipping fast, and the bottleneck is serving—latency, cost, reliability. Two questions: where do you run inference today, and what breaks first—cost or tail latency? Cool. Let me show you the experience.”
[20:17] Soojin Lee: Much better.
[20:19] Markus Klein: Then I hit run and stream.

[20:22] Avery Johnson: Perfect.

[20:24] (brief crosstalk)
[20:26] Soojin Lee: One more nuance: when we say “Dedicated,” define it. People assume “single tenant” means “physically isolated.”
[20:34] Avery Johnson: We can say “reserved GPU pool with predictable throughput and isolation.”
[20:40] Markus Klein: And for private: “customer-managed networking, private control plane options.”

[20:46] Avery Johnson: Great. We’ll keep it honest.

[20:49] Markus Klein: On the tenant side: we need parallel demos support. Otherwise two AEs collide.
[20:55] Avery Johnson: Yeah, that happened last week.
[20:57] Soojin Lee: Add a rule: each demo gets its own project + key.
[21:02] Markus Klein: Provisioning automation will do that.

[21:06] Avery Johnson: Cool. Also: demo certification checklist.
[21:10] Soojin Lee: Not on this call, but yes we’ll need it.

[21:13] Markus Klein: Anything else on objections.
[21:16] Avery Johnson: Pricing confusion: usage vs commits.
[21:20] Soojin Lee: Don’t go deep. Say: “Hosted is usage-based, Dedicated is reserved capacity, Private is license/support.”
[21:28] Avery Johnson: Done.

[21:31] Markus Klein: Alright, I’ll take ownership on the healthcheck and simplifying tool calling.
[21:37] Avery Johnson: I’ll rewrite the first minutes and create a 20-min variant.
[21:42] Soojin Lee: I’ll update talk track language and add handoff cues.

[21:47] Avery Johnson: Anything else we should capture.
[21:50] Markus Klein: Make sure the time range in dashboards defaults to something sane for the demo.
[21:55] Soojin Lee: If product can’t change fast, at least put it in run-of-show: “switch to last 24 hours.”
[22:01] Avery Johnson: Yep.

[22:04] Markus Klein: Also: have a “known-good” model list pinned for demos.
[22:08] Avery Johnson: And a safe fallback policy.
[22:10] Soojin Lee: Great.

[22:12] Avery Johnson: Okay, we can stop the recording? Or do we want to keep riffing.
[22:17] Markus Klein: I think we got what we need.
[22:19] Soojin Lee: Yeah. Send me the action items, I’ll update the doc.

[22:24] Avery Johnson: Cool. End.

(Recording continued - post-meeting chatter)
[22:31] Markus Klein: I’m going to drop a note: the rollouts screen is okay today but it’s been flaky.
[22:37] Soojin Lee: Screenshot it anyway.
[22:39] Avery Johnson: Yep.

[22:42] Markus Klein: Also, I’ll clean up the demo app. Right now it has three scenarios and it’s confusing.
[22:48] Soojin Lee: One scenario in the default view.
[22:50] Avery Johnson: Exactly.

[22:52] Markus Klein: Alright, I’m out.
[22:54] Soojin Lee: Thanks.
[22:56] Avery Johnson: Thanks all.
